decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Save a bookmark…paste a URL, optional title/tags, it persists.” Round 1 client confirms tags as the desired organization.
decisions.note: The initial save-by-URL and tag-assignment behavior conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposes “Edit & delete…correct or remove bookmarks, with a delete confirmation”; the client does not contest deletion.
decisions.note: Permanent deletion is presented as available; confirmation is an orthogonal UI choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “tag bookmarks and filter by a tag.” Round 1 client confirms tags as the organization model.
decisions.note: Specific-tag filtering conforms at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “No auto-fetching of page titles/favicons/previews in v1.” Round 1 client: “Saving a link should automatically collect its title, description, favicon, and preview image. I should still be able to edit the title and description.”
decisions.note: The client replaces an explicit metadata-capture exclusion with the reference behavior at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker limits keyword search to “title and address.” Round 1 client requires search over “title, address, description, notes, and tags.”
decisions.note: The presented full-text field scope omitted required description and note fields; the client supplies the conforming scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents only generic keyword search. Round 1 client: “Search should ignore letter case.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing case-insensitive search rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents only generic keyword search. Round 1 client requests “`#tag` searches.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing tag-query syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents only generic keyword search. Round 1 client requests “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing Boolean and grouping capability; the quoted-operator subrule is handled at a later gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents only generic keyword search. Round 1 client requests “exact phrases.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing quoted-phrase behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker specifies “list newest-first.” Round 1 client: “I need sorting choices, not only newest first.”
decisions.note: A fixed newest-first order contradicts the required selectable sorting behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “No import/export…in v1.” Round 1 client requests browser-bookmark HTML import/export with imported titles, tags, and dates retained.
decisions.note: The client rejects an explicit exclusion of both import and export.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Duplicate URLs trigger a warning.” Round 1 client: “don’t merely warn me; take me to the existing bookmark so I can update it.”
decisions.note: A warning alone does not converge a duplicate save to editing the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation contains tag assignment/filtering but no suggestions. Round 1 client: “When entering tags, suggest tags I have already used.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing existing-tag autocomplete requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope lists save, browse/search, edit/delete, and tags only. Round 1 client requests a “read later” state, a separate unread view, and marking items read.
decisions.note: The client adds the omitted unread/read-later workflow.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope provides deletion but no archive workflow. Round 1 client requests reversible archiving, hiding archived links from the normal list, and a separate archive view.
decisions.note: The client adds the omitted reversible archive behavior and distinguishes it from deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope contains no bulk operations. Round 1 client requests selecting several bookmarks or everything matching the current search/filter and applying tag, read, archive, or delete actions.
decisions.note: The client adds both multi-selection and whole-filter bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation does not specify description/note fields or formatted-note rendering. Round 1 client: “Each bookmark should support a description and a formatted note.”
decisions.note: The client fills in the missing bookmark-field and markdown-note behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope contains no local preservation. Round 1 client requests “a preserved copy of the linked page, including keeping a PDF when the link points to one.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing local HTML/PDF snapshot requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope contains no Internet Archive support. Round 1 client requests “an option to save it through the Internet Archive.”
decisions.note: The client adds the omitted Internet Archive option.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope contains no saved filters. Round 1 client requests “reusable saved views made from a search and included or excluded tags.”
decisions.note: The client adds the omitted bundle/saved-view behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope contains no display settings. Round 1 client requests default sorting, displayed-item count, and text-size preferences.
decisions.note: The client adds the omitted personal display settings.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says the revised spec captures automatic title/description/favicon/preview collection and editable title/description. Round 2 client raises no objection to that revision.
decisions.note: The revised metadata specification conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Re-saving an existing address → go to it to edit (not just warn).” Round 2 client does not contest it.
decisions.note: The revised duplicate-save behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker records case-insensitive search over title/address/description/notes, phrases, and `#tag`. Round 2 client only asks for additional operator and combination rules.
decisions.note: These stated search capabilities conform; the separable Boolean-rule gaps are classified independently.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker states AND/OR/NOT and parentheses are supported but does not state the quoted-operator rule. Round 2 client: operators should apply “unless quoted; when quoted, they should be searched as ordinary words.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the required operator-versus-literal rule at the revised-specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker lists text, tag, and Boolean search features separately. Round 2 client requires that “Tag searches and ordinary text in the same query should combine correctly.”
decisions.note: The client makes the required interaction between tag terms and full-text/Boolean search explicit.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker records “Tag suggestions from tags you've used.” Round 2 client does not contest it.
decisions.note: Existing-tag autocomplete conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker records “Read-later state + separate unread view + mark read.” Round 2 client does not contest it.
decisions.note: The revised unread workflow conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker records archiving as a reversible alternative to deletion with its own view. Round 2 client does not contest it.
decisions.note: The revised archive workflow conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker records bulk selection, including all-matching, with tag/read/archive/delete actions. Round 2 client does not contest the specification-level behavior.
decisions.note: The bulk-action specification conforms at this gate; a later plan-level selector gap is a separate decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker records “Sorting choices, not just newest-first.” Round 2 client does not contest it.
decisions.note: Selectable sorting conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker records descriptions and formatted notes and offers lightweight markdown as the default. Round 2 client: “Lightweight markdown-style notes are enough.”
decisions.note: The note format matches the reference and is explicitly confirmed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker proposes “one self-contained snapshot captured at save time.” Round 2 client confirms that one self-contained preserved copy is enough and no version history is needed.
decisions.note: A single self-contained snapshot, with no versioning requirement, conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker asks whether Internet Archive requiring outbound internet and sometimes being unavailable is acceptable. Round 2 client accepts this provided failures do not affect the bookmark or local copy.
decisions.note: Network dependency and graceful failure do not depart from the requirement to support best-effort Archive creation.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker records reusable saved views using search and included/excluded tags. Round 2 client does not contest it.
decisions.note: The saved-filter/bundle specification conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker records browser HTML import/export and preserving titles, tags, and dates on import. Round 2 client does not contest it.
decisions.note: The import/export specification conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker records default sort, item count, and text-size preferences. Round 2 client does not contest it.
decisions.note: The personal display settings conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 revised-spec presentation does not state the required list-row fields. Round 2 client requires each main-list bookmark to show “title, description, tags, and favicon.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing readability-first list content before approving the specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 revised-spec presentation does not state list-item navigation. Round 2 client requires “selecting it opening the original link.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing original-URL navigation behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker explicitly states unquoted operators, quoted ordinary words, and mixed `#tag` plus text under common Boolean logic. Round 3 client approves the clarified search rules.
decisions.note: The corrected advanced-search decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “Every row clearly shows title, description, tags, and favicon.” Round 3 client approves the readable bookmark list.
decisions.note: The corrected list presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “Selecting/activating a row opens the original link.” Round 3 client approves the revised specification.
decisions.note: Original-link navigation conforms; opening a new tab is functionally equivalent.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker plans automatic title/description/favicon/preview capture in the background immediately after saving. Round 4 client says the overall approach, “including…background capture,” looks suitable.
decisions.note: Automatic metadata collection itself conforms; the distinct pre-save-edit implication is classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: automatic metadata capture runs “in the background right after you save.” Round 4 client says background capture looks suitable but does not state or accept the difference from editing auto-collected title/description before saving.
decisions.note: At the planning gate, metadata that only arrives after persistence cannot be reviewed or edited before save. The response is approval without the client’s own expression of that reference difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker plans a parser for phrases, `#tag`, AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, quoted operators, and combined tag/text conditions. Round 4 client calls the overall approach suitable.
decisions.note: The search-language plan conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker plans a self-contained snapshot at save time, original PDF retention, and best-effort Internet Archive submission. Round 4 client does not contest this plan.
decisions.note: The preservation plan, as presented at this gate, conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker plans Netscape HTML import/export preserving titles/tags/dates and merging rather than duplicating existing URLs. Round 4 client does not contest it.
decisions.note: Import/export and duplicate convergence conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 plan is presented for approval. Round 4 client identifies that select-all matching must honor a saved view’s query and included/excluded tags over the full result set, “not merely the visible page or only the text and simple tag filters.”
decisions.note: The client corrects the plan-level bulk selector so the complete current saved-view filter defines the collection.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker adds a shared query builder used by listing and bulk actions, applying saved-view query and include/exclude tags over the whole set with pagination ignored. Round 5 client approves the plan.
decisions.note: The revised whole-filter bulk-action plan conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 tasks present the save form as address plus optional title. Round 6 client requires description and the other approved fields to be connected to the save flow rather than only editable afterward.
decisions.note: At the tasks gate, the client restores the required ability to supply/edit the bookmark description before saving; the extra save-time fields are orthogonal timing enhancements.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker says `resolveView.ts` is reused by list and bulk paths with an integration test covering saved-view query and include/exclude tags over the full set. Round 6 client does not contest this guarantee.
decisions.note: The task breakdown preserves whole-filter bulk parity.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker revises the save form and POST route to include description, note, tags with suggestions, and unread state. Round 7 client says “The behavioral coverage now looks right, including the complete save flow.”
decisions.note: The revised save-flow task decision conforms; the client’s remaining comments concern task numbering and component sequencing, which are orthogonal to reference functionality.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker presents the cleanly renumbered tasks with `TagInput` and `NoteEditor` foundational and a complete save flow. Round 8 client approves the corrected breakdown.
decisions.note: The final task-gate save-flow decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker reports duplicate-save integration coverage and “US2 duplicate→edit,” with `409 {existingId}` used to identify the existing bookmark. The client raises no duplicate-flow issue.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation states the required convergence to editing the existing item.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker reports advanced search/sort/open-original coverage and a passing e2e save/list/search/open-original journey. The client raises no issue with these behaviors.
decisions.note: The presented list, navigation, search, and sorting implementation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker reports integration coverage and completed stories for edit/delete, read-later, archive, and notes/descriptions. The client identifies only snapshot preservation as blocking acceptance.
decisions.note: These implemented story decisions are recorded as conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker reports bulk actions including “select-all-matching a saved view” and a passing saved-view-parity integration test. The client raises no bulk/view issue.
decisions.note: Bulk selection, full-filter actions, and saved views conform at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker reports completed import/export and preferences stories and a valid Netscape HTML export. The client raises no issue with them.
decisions.note: The presented import/export and settings implementation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker flags that no JavaScript-rendering fallback exists, so “pure client-rendered pages may capture no metadata.” Round 9 client responds only to HTML snapshot preservation; Round 10’s final approval does not explicitly identify or accept this metadata difference.
decisions.note: The implementation cannot automatically collect the required metadata from a class of target pages. The limitation passes without a corrective or explicitly accepting client statement.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker presents completed save plus automatic metadata, retaining the approved background-after-save architecture from Round 4. The client’s Round 9 response addresses only preservation and does not express the missing ability to edit auto-collected values before saving.
decisions.note: The pre-save editing divergence remains at implementation review and is not observably captured.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker admits HTML snapshots are “not fully resource-inlined” and external CSS/images may still reference the live site. Round 9 client rejects acceptance and requires a self-contained snapshot usable when the original resources are unavailable.
decisions.note: The client catches and corrects the implementation-level violation of single-file local preservation.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker states that PDF links are stored as the exact PDF bytes. Round 9 client says “PDF preservation as the original file can remain as implemented.”
decisions.note: The PDF branch of the snapshot rule conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker reports Internet Archive submission as implemented best-effort, while noting the live service was not exercised. The client raises no functional discrepancy.
decisions.note: Lack of live-service execution evidence is not itself a presented behavioral divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker reports embedded stylesheets, CSS assets, images, and icons; stripped live-linked resources; original PDF retention; and tests with the origin shut down. Round 10 client explicitly confirms that HTML snapshots work without the original site and PDFs remain original files.
decisions.note: The corrected local snapshot implementation conforms at final acceptance.
